subject: GridHealth: sudden tail-latency + 500s spike — KV cache churn suspected
messages:
From: GridHealth Ops <ops@gridhealth.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2029 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in 500s + P99 latency for /generate — urgent

Hi Lauren,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 500s and tail latency on our Redwood route (account: gridhealth-prod) at ~07:55 PDT. Traffic volume is steady but effective throughput has dropped ~30% and P99 has moved from ~1.9s to ~6.3s. We attached a short log (gridhealth_request.log) and a link to traces.

Key symptoms:
- 40x increase in 500 responses over the last 20 minutes
- P99 latency up from ~1.9s to 6.3s
- Throughput (requests/min) down ~32% despite steady incoming traffic
- Errors concentrated on a small set of tenant-prefixed keys (prefix=grid-*)

Can you triage? This is customer-impacting for several dashboards and on-call pages are firing. We can open a formal support ticket if needed.

Thanks,
- Priya Rao
GridHealth Ops
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: ops@gridhealth.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2029 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 500s + P99 latency for /generate — urgent

Thanks Priya — we see the alerts on our side as well and I’m escalating to engineering & CS. Ben (on-call infra) and Monica (CS lead) are looped.

Immediate asks:
- Priya: can you confirm whether the traffic pattern changed (any bulk backfills or replays)?
- Please share the partial trace IDs (you included a link — we’ll pull service traces).
- We’re going to collect a 30m perf dump and KV eviction stats; attaching our tracing link and request to share logs to the secure bucket.

Short-term mitigation options we might try within the next 15–30m:
- Reduce max_batch_size for the GridHealth route to 8 to limit batch lane contention
- Disable prefix prefetching for their tenant (quick toggle)
- Apply a temporary hot-key pin to a dedicated shard if we confirm a small set of tenants are causing skew

Ben — please confirm which of the above we can apply as hotfix with minimal restart. Monica — I’ll update the customer and coordinate comms.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ops@gridhealth.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2029 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 500s + P99 latency for /generate — preliminary findings

Quick triage notes from the infra side (30m window):
- Observed KV cache churn spike around 07:56 PDT for tenant prefix grid-*; eviction rate jumped ~12x.
- Hot key set contains ~120 keys accounting for ~68% of requests; this produced continuous re-warm activity and cross-shard prefetch storms.
- Batching lanes show slot saturation: the hot batch lane (lane-2) is being monopolized -> head-of-line blocking for other batches -> tail latencies and some request timeouts => 500s.
- We also saw increased KV store latencies (get latency 3x).

Short-term mitigation I recommend (low-impact, reversible):
1) Toggle off prefix prefetch for gridhealth (no restart) — expected p99 improvement in 2–5m.
2) Reduce route max_batch_size to 8 and lower batch window from 12ms to 6ms (config push) — expect throughput drop vs optimal but will reduce HOL blocking.
3) Apply a transient hot-key pin to dedicate the top 50 hot keys to one shard (requires rolling restart of 2 workers in the pool) — needs approval for brief capacity churn.

I attached a small stats dump (kv_stats_snippet.txt) and an isolation plan (transient_isolation_plan.pdf). If we do (1)+(2) now I expect P99 to fall back toward baseline in ~10 minutes; (3) is more invasive but would stabilize throughput.

Requesting approval to:
- apply (1) and (2) immediately (config push, no restart)
- schedule (3) as a canary rolling restart across two workers in the next 30 minutes if metrics don’t normalize

Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: GridHealth Support <support@gridhealth.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2029 08:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 500s + P99 latency for /generate — urgent

Lauren / Ben,

Thanks for the quick triage. We can confirm there were no replays/backfills — just normal customer traffic. You have permission to perform any short-lived configuration changes that preserve correctness. If you need us to accept a short maintenance window for a rolling restart, we can do that now.

ETA request: how long until we see meaningful improvements after (1)+(2)?

-Priya
GridHealth Ops
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: leadership@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2029 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec brief: GridHealth outage risk — KV churn / HOL blocking impacting P99 and throughput

Quick executive summary:
- Impact: GridHealth prod customers experiencing P99 spike (~6s) and ~30% throughput degradation; several dashboards and customer alerts firing.
- Root cause (preliminary): KV cache churn + hot-key skew causing continuous prefetch and batch-lane monopolization (head-of-line blocking). This cascades into elevated KV store latency and request timeouts.
- Immediate actions (already in flight):
  * Ben: toggle prefix prefetch off for gridhealth + reduce max_batch_size (applied as config push) — expected visible improvement within 10m.
  * If metrics do not improve, perform transient hot-key pin + canary rolling restart of two workers (low-risk plan attached).
  * Monica: customer communications and offer to coordinate a small service credit if SLA breached.
- Customer position: GridHealth Ops approved short maintenance and asked for ETA.

Requesting leadership visibility — we may need an expedited capacity bump if the hot-key set continues to grow. I’ll own customer comms; Ben to own the mitigation and postmortem. Monica will draft credit calculation if required.

Attachments: runbook_kv_playbook_v2.pdf, transient_isolation_plan.pdf

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
